name: Facade Quality and Street-Wall Continuity (Beijing)
description: Method replication: the images are new Baidu street views of Beijing, not the paper's stimuli. Raters score 20 street views for the construction and maintenance quality of building facades (1–4 rubric) and judge for 20 more whether the street wall is continuous, using the rubrics of Liu, Silva, Wu & Wang (2017, CEUS). Differences from the original study: (1) the two judgements draw their images independently instead of using the same image; (2) the on-site survey of passers-by is not included.
author: Liu, Silva, Wu & Wang

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: facade_quality
elements.title: Rate the construction and maintenance quality of the building facade.
rateLabels: 1 – Built with low-quality materials, in many cases bare cement and colour plate; low-level precision, sometimes unfinished; seriously deteriorated with a lot of cracks, breakage, corrosion, dirt and stain or messy add-ons.
2 – Built with low quality, not very fine-textured materials; low-level industrial precision or craftsmanship; a lot of cracks, breakage, corrosion, dirt and stain or messy add-ons.

3 – Built with lower quality, not very fine-textured materials; no high level of industrial precision or craftsmanship; may have a few obvious cracks, breakage, corrosion, dirt and stain or messy add-ons but generally a neat and clean look.

4 – Built with high quality, fine-textured materials; high industrial precision or fine craftsmanship (components and material pieces well aligned, small gaps); well maintained without obvious cracks, breakage, corrosion, dirt and stain or messy add-ons.

elements.name: street_wall_continuity
elements.title: Is the street wall continuous?
elements.description: Continuous: Building facades progress through the image without any interruption, blockage or significant setback, at least at the eye height. Discontinuous: There is a wide gap between two adjacent buildings; there is a significant setback of a wide building; or there is a solid wall blocking the building from the street. If the wall is carefully designed and visually attractive, it can be considered continuous.
